end.summary:
Observed and described beaks, feet, and leaf shapes.
Discussed duck feet, chicken feet, woodpecker beaks, and gripping claws.
Explored how webbed feet help push water and wide feet help on snow.
Discussed thin, waxy, broad, and thorn-like leaves in relation to water and habitat.
Teach-back was not passed; feature-to-function links needed further practice.
end.parentNote: Atharv practised noticing plant and animal features and explaining what those features may help with. They used examples such as webbed feet pushing water, claws helping a bird grip, and lotus leaves staying on water. Some links between leaf features and habitats were still mixed, and they were not corrected later in the lesson. At home, look at one plant or bird together and ask: “What do you notice, and how might that feature help it?”
